codeReview.summary: Clean implementation of weighted rotation algorithm for proxy selection. The code adds get_weight() to ProxyStats (returns 0 for cooldown, 50 for new, success_rate otherwise), select_weighted_proxy() using cumulative weight distribution, and modifies get_next_proxy() to use weighted selection when weights differ, falling back to round-robin when equal. 18 unit tests cover weight calculation, equal-weights detection, weighted selection distribution, and edge cases. All 162 tests pass including the 7 weighted-specific filtered tests.

issues.description: pseudo_random() uses SystemTime::now().subsec_nanos() which is not cryptographically random and can produce predictable sequences when called in rapid succession (e.g., within the same nanosecond). For proxy selection this is acceptable — true randomness is not required, only statistical weighting. However, if get_next_proxy() is called in a tight loop, the same proxy could be selected repeatedly. The test test_proxy_pool_weighted_selection_favors_higher_weight mitigates this by running 1000 iterations, suggesting adequate entropy in practice. No action required for the current use case.

When total_weight is 0 (all proxies have 0% success rate and none are in cooldown), select_weighted_proxy() falls back to returning available[0]. This is a reasonable fallback but means a consistently failing proxy always gets selected. An alternative would be to fall back to round-robin in this case. Not blocking since this edge case is unlikely in practice (bad proxies with 3+ consecutive failures are already excluded from available list).

summary: Weighted rotation implementation is correct and well-tested. The algorithm properly weights proxies by success rate, excludes cooldown proxies (weight 0), gives new proxies a neutral weight of 50, and falls back to round-robin when all weights are equal. 18 unit tests provide good coverage including statistical distribution verification. Both VAL-HLT-011 (higher success rate = more frequent selection) and VAL-CRS-004 (recovery flow integration via cooldown weight exclusion) are fulfilled. Two non-blocking observations noted about pseudo-random entropy in tight loops and the zero-total-weight fallback behavior.
